newsitem.title: USA: Dell slumps on downgrade, weighs on group.
newsitem.headline: Dell slumps on downgrade, weighs on group.

text.p: Shares in Dell Computer Corp skidded lower early Monday, leading a stiff sell-off among personal computer shares for the second straight session.
Dell, whose month-long rally had spearheaded a sharp advance among PC stocks, fell 3-5/8 to 77-7/8 in the first trading since the company's two-for-one stock split took effect.
The sell-off followed a downgrade by Bear Stearns analyst Andrew Neff, who voiced concern over Dell's lofty valuation.
It also extended a sharp decline posted last Friday when Dell's pre-split shares dropped seven points to 163.
Traders said Dell's weak showing was casting a pall over the entire group.
"It's leading the pack down," said Ken Ducey, director of trading at BT Brokerage. "These stocks are in very nervous hands, and a lot of them probably have profits they're trying to nail down."
Compaq Computer Corp fell 4-3/4 to 130-7/8, Gateway 2000 Inc dipped 11/16 to 39-11/16, and International Business Machines Corp lost 1-5/16 to 105-11/16.
Hewlett-Packard Co bucked the trend, gaining 13/16 to 66-5/16.

The selling pressure came amid new signs that the top-tier computer sellers are enjoying robust sales growth. According to reports by industry research groups International Data Corp and Dataquest, worldwide personal computer sales grew a solid 16 to 17 percent in the second quarter.

The top four vendors -- Compaq, IBM, H-P and Dell -- all had unit growth rates that vastly outpaced the rest of the industry. Of the four, H-P produced the only major surprise, leaping to third place in the rankings from sixth a year ago.
Bear Stearns analyst Neff said he was not calling into question the strong fundamentals of the industry or even Dell, just the high valuation that Dell's recent share price had implied.

"The issue was, Dell was selling at a multiple toward the high end of its P-E (price-to-earnings) and growth rate ranges," Neff said. "This was purely based on valuation. The fundamentals at Dell remain strong."
Neff now rates Dell an "accumulate." He declined to say at what price he thought Dell would again warrant a "buy" rating.
Dell shares racked up a sizzling 48.6 percent in gains between July 1 and July 24. The two-day downturn has pared that to about 37 percent.
The story was similar for Compaq, which surged some 38 percent from July 1 to July 24. Losses in the last two sessions have cut the figure to 29 percent.
